organization_creation.provider_constraint: Provider6.68.0 Create unconditionally calls EnablePolicyType for every configured entry. Native CreateOrganization ALL already enables SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY, and repeating that call correctly fails with PolicyTypeAlreadyEnabledException.
organization_creation.fixture_sequence: Targeted Terraform creation of the organization with bootstrap=true and no explicitly requested policy types, followed by a full apply with bootstrap=false. That update retains the native default SCP and enables TAG_POLICY from the real read state. All later refresh, import and update stages use the full desired policy set. No errors or drift are suppressed.
organization_creation.trusted_access: The organization's aggregate desired principal list includes account.amazonaws.com for the provider's real Account Management PutAccountName update, ram.amazonaws.com for RAM organization sharing, and sso.amazonaws.com for standalone SSO trusted access. These are required live owner prerequisites, not plan drift to ignore.
organization_creation.failure_cleanup: Initial apply and each native seed are guarded. Dependent controls must destroy successfully before organization membership or native identity seeds are removed; failed controls cleanup preserves those prerequisites for normal recovery. Cleanup errors remain attached to the original failure. Removed external accounts and their real IAM identity remain independent native accounts, not fake deleted accounts.

organizations: Fixture creates ALL features, two OUs, two accounts, SCP and TAG_POLICY attachments, current delegation, standalone root tag and all 14 direct data-source types.

Member default access roles issue real STS credentials; isolated S3 discovery, current SCP rejection and account-name/parent updates are required. A separately seeded external account uses a custom role name and real provisioning.
GovCloud create_govcloud=true is unimplemented. close_on_deletion=true currently changes organization metadata without coordinated registry/downstream closure; do not claim real account closure.
Other policy types, billing access, invitation/all-feature transitions, quotas and all IAM condition combinations are not exercised by this fixture.
Terraform imports cannot reconstruct the create-only custom role_name or billing flag from native account reads; the managed-account fixture uses their omitted defaults, not ignore_changes.
ram: Fixture covers all eight direct types, including accepted external invitation, organization sharing, individual associations, an exclusive association set and custom permission versions.
Signed member and external SSM reads must return actual advanced parameter values. An unshared member must be denied.

SSM parameters do not support recipient withdrawal. Cleanup first disassociates the external share's resource as the owner, verifies no associated resources remain, then normally destroys the Terraform accepter and dependent controls before organization membership. Deleted RAM tombstones are asserted explicitly.
The live EC2 subnet and CodeBuild project consumers are not exercised here. Missing other resource owners stay unsupported.

Updated custom permission versions are checked by Terraform reads; propagation of the new version to already associated shares is not proved by common GetParameter consumer calls. Permission-specific controls and resource-owner types beyond these fixtures remain unverified.
ssoadmin: Fixture covers permission sets, inline/managed/customer policies, boundary, individual and exclusive attachments, group account assignments and all three implemented directory/permission-set data sources.

Assignments provision actual protected IAM roles in management and member accounts. A real Cognito password/device-form flow issues SSO portal credentials; signed STS and S3 requests, role duration updates and current directory membership removal must prove enforcement.
The HTTP form consumer is not an AWS CLI or real-browser parity test. Existing documented device/PKCE browser workflows remain separate.

Applications, ABAC, trusted token issuers and multi-region owners remain unimplemented. Customer-managed instance KMS settings, disabled permission sets and ProvisioningStatus filters are unsupported.
sso: No direct Terraform resource or data-source types. The SSO SDK/endpoint is a real credential-consumer prerequisite for the SSO Admin fixture.
ssooidc: No direct Terraform resource or data-source types. Public RegisterClient, StartDeviceAuthorization and CreateToken plus actual Cognito authorization form are fixture prerequisites. CreateTokenWithIAM/application-entitled registration are unsupported.
cloudformation: Fixture covers stack resource, stack/export/type data sources, captured default AWS registry schema discovery, native S3/SQS/SSM resources, SSM version references and ImportValue dependencies.
Actual binary S3/SQS transfer and native parameter values are required after create/update/restart. Secure dynamic-reference source and redacted attributes are preserved without changes.
StackSets and private extension registration/execution are not implemented. DescribeType does not claim that every captured AWS schema has a local resource owner.

DescribeType exposes only captured default AWS-owned resource schemas. Private registrations, historical VersionId and third-party PublisherId/PublicVersionNumber selectors are not available. DefaultVersionId stays absent for public AWS types.
Stack resource options and other native resource families remain bounded by their existing owners; this fixture does not prove every property, role, policy, import/refactoring or transform branch.
cloudcontrol: Fixture covers resource and data source with the default provider DescribeType dependency, real SSM owner create/read/patch-update/delete and restart. No explicit supplied schema masks that dependency.
Terraform AWS 6.68.0 aws_cloudcontrolapi_resource has no importer; do not invent an import path. Other cohort resources exercise import.
Other owner types, role_arn delegation, type_version_id, all JSON Patch operators and write-only settings are not exercised. Missing owners/custom registry types are not synthesized.
resourcegroups: Terraform covers TAG_FILTERS_1_0 query groups plus aws_resourcegroups_resource against an actual AppRegistry application group. Provider6.68.0 rejects CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_1_0 in its schema, so stack-query create/read/update/reopen/membership/delete is an explicitly native SDK supplement. Live native S3/SQS/SSM membership and the actual SQS awsApplication tag must agree.
Stack queries continue to require private native incarnation claims. No public marker or stack history is used as resource ownership.

Specialty EC2 group configurations and query/resource families without existing owner adapters remain unsupported. Remaining query filters, pagination, lifecycle/tag-sync and SSM targeting paths are not exercised here.

Compliance/history/report generation and cross-account/all-owner tagging paths remain separately implemented but unverified by this Terraform fixture. No copied resource/tag catalog is added.
servicecatalogappregistry: All six direct types are in the fixture. Application grouping changes the actual SQS owner tag and Resource Groups membership. Attribute JSON updates and associations are read by the provider.

The pinned provider resends unchanged names for description/attribute updates; these must remain idempotent and reach the existing authorized update path. Actual application/attribute-group name changes remain unsupported and are not exercised.
Native AWS positive application creation is not claimed; retained native evidence reports maintenance-mode rejection. This fixture is local only.
CFN_STACK/RESOURCE_TAG_VALUE resource association, tag-sync, service-role revocation and additional application-resource owner families are not exercised here.
